summary.headline: Suzlon Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR3,819 crores and PAT was INR305 crores, with EBITDA flat at INR595 crores on upfront 2.0 costs and deferred deliveries.
summary.overview: Suzlon delivered a record first-quarter 506 MW, with consolidated revenue of INR3,819 crores (+23% YoY), EBITDA of INR595 crores (flat vs INR599 crores) and PAT of INR305 crores. Management attributed the flat margin to Middle East–linked logistics disruptions that deferred an estimated 10–20% of deliveries, higher fixed costs for Suzlon 2.0 (Puducherry facility, leadership, technology, marketing) and a mix shift toward lower-margin EPC/RE solutions versus AMS. Commissioning (COD) rose to 269 MW from 117 MW, with about 1,257 MW erected but awaiting commissioning. Order book stands at 6.1 GW, with about 1 GW booked in the first four months of FY27, of which 600-plus MW is DevCo-led.

segments.name: WTG / RE Solutions
segments.commentary: Q1 deliveries of 506 MW and ASP of INR6.3 crore per MW, lifted by a higher EPC share (32% vs 22% a year ago) and project business. Management said the EBIT per MW fell from INR26 lakh to INR52 lakh (as stated on the call, figures as quoted by the analyst).

segments.name: RE AMS (O&M)
segments.commentary: Management cited a 43% EBITDA margin this quarter, which it said is elevated and should settle in the high 30s to about 40%. Installed base is 16.1+ GW in India with machine availability consistently above 95%.

segments.name: Foundry and forgings
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR126 crores and EBITDA of INR22 crores; the business is pursuing three segments (foundry, forging, bearing) and aims to raise non-Suzlon, non-wind and export share, but is exposed to Gulf-related customer disruption.

guidance_outlook: Suzlon 2.0 targets 25% CAGR over the next five years.
EBITDA margin guided at 17–18% range, plus or minus 1–2% for FY27, with operating leverage expected to help in H2.
Q1 fixed-cost upfront impact estimated at INR40–50 crores; management said it is a year-long journey, not a one-quarter item.
Seasonality holds: historically about 35–40% of deliveries in H1 and 60–65% in H2.
Capex guidance of about INR700 crores, plus or minus INR100 crores, excluding DevCo investment.
DevCo investment capped at INR500 crores on a revolving basis; currently INR200–300 crores deployed.
FY31 ambition of 10 GW RE sales (75:25 wind to solar/BESS split, i.e., 7.5 GW wind) and 3.1 GW BESS target by FY31; annual installations seen crossing 10 GW near term and 15 GW by FY31.
Management expects a confirmed repowering order book in India before end-FY27.
Market pricing described as healthy; ASP expected to stay in fairly good range as project share rises.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity is 4.5 GW, fully operational, with 3 AI-enabled smart factories; new AI-enabled blade factories are being built in India for 5 MW and S163 platforms.
Erected but not commissioned turbines stood at about 1,257 MW at quarter end, which management expects to lift future CODs.

S175 (5 MW) launched in India with a first domestic order; deliveries to start end of this year and in the following year. S163 (6.3 MW) is for international markets, with an 18–24 month lead time to seed a market.
Capex of about INR700 crores (plus or minus INR100 crores), excluding DevCo land and connectivity investment.
Solar serviceable asset base of 20+ GW identified within 25 km of Suzlon service locations.
demand_pricing: Order book of 6.1 GW; about 1 GW secured in first four months of FY27; DevCo accounts for about 60% of new orders (600-plus MW booked in four months).
Indian bid pipeline is about 5 GW; management said demand is not the constraint, execution is.
Mix: order book largely S144 3 series, with about 2 GW of retail/other orders; PSU and C&I make up about 85% of the order book.

Export opportunities under evaluation in Europe, Australia, Latin America and Southeast Asia; management said Suzlon competes on value and energy yield rather than price against Chinese and two-to-three large global OEMs.
Domestic pricing described as 'more or less same' despite INR depreciation; cost pressure offset by volume ramp and supplier diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a large gap between 506 MW deliveries and 269 MW COD, and when will erected inventory convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the RR-versus-COD gap will persist but should narrow as erection completes; seasonality (35–40% H1, 60–65% H2) is expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the EBITDA margin weakness and per-MW EBIT decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat EBITDA reflects upfront Suzlon 2.0 investments, lower deliveries from geopolitical disruption (operating leverage) and mix toward RE solutions from higher-margin AMS.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the WTG fixed cost is one-time, and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the upfront impact is about INR40–50 crores across subheads; the company still targets 17–18% EBITDA margin, plus or minus 1–2%.

qa_highlights.question: Are DevCo sales margin-accretive, and what advances have been received?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 602 MW DevCo EPC contracts have the same commercial terms as past deals, with faster execution because land and connectivity are ready, and that the advances are value accretive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest expense increase and tax outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed higher interest to higher working capital utilisation and revenue growth, partly offset by lower average borrowing rates. Tax charges are non-cash deferred-tax asset run-downs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10 GW FY31 sales ambition achievable with 4.5 GW capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY31 target is 10 GW RE sales (75% wind = 7.5 GW) and that current 4.5 GW capacity can be stepped up through migration to higher-rated turbines, with capacity expansion planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital and receivables trend as EPC share rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC does not structurally worsen working capital, that receivables are improving and that payment terms are priced into contracts.

risks_watch: Recovery of 10–20% of deferred deliveries in coming quarters, plus conversion of about 1,257 MW of erected turbines into commissioning.
Sustained fixed-cost ramp for Suzlon 2.0 and whether the 17–18% EBITDA margin band holds.
Cash conversion: PSU/C&I dominated order book and DevCo working-capital draw (INR200–300 crores of INR500 crores cap).
Geopolitical and logistics disruption (fuel, cranes, trailers) affecting West Asia-linked supply chains.
Export strategy costs and timing of S163 international ramp; 18–24 month market seeding lead time.
Repowering order confirmation expected before end-FY27; BESS partnerships expected to close in the next couple of months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and long-term targets, but defensive on near-term margins, attributing the flat EBITDA to one-time and upfront costs. Management was evasive on specific quantifications (foreign holding caps, fixed-cost full-year figures, export spend) and gave few hard numbers beyond the INR40–50 crore one-time estimate.
key_quotes: Suzlon delivered 506 megawatts in Q1, making our highest ever first quarter deliveries.
Order book is not a constraint with DevCo model in place with 60% new orders from DevCo.
So we're very happy to partner with both of them.

growth.why: Management guides to 25% CAGR for Suzlon 2.0 over five years and 17-18% FY27 EBITDA margin (+/-1-2%), backed by a 6.1 GW order book, about 1 GW booked in four months, 1,257 MW erected awaiting commissioning, and a 4.5 GW manufacturing base; capacity additions are new blade factories and S175 launch, with no specific timelines or numbers for the new capacity.
